trust_decision.summary: Strings that come from Caddy traffic (access-log URI/host/method/raw line, per-host metric label, FrankenPHP in-flight request, certificate names, error text) are untrusted and must have C0/DEL/C1 control bytes stripped before they are written to the operator's terminal. The published fix decides this at the TUI render boundary (internal/ui), not at parse time.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'from Caddy logs ... injected into the TUI'. formatLogRow renders access-log Method/Host/URI/RawLine through fitCellLeft (internal/ui/logtable.go:282-326), and an engineer reaches it first.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: internal/ui/app.go:366-368 (status/error line wraps .Error() text that echoes external bytes); also internal/ui/certificates.go:90-106 (certificate subject/issuer, which are not logs)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about Caddy *logs*. The status line shows ember's own error messages, certificate names come from TLS rather than logs, and `ember diff` only reads the operator's own JSON files (which are 'already JSON-escaped'), so none of these look like log-injection surfaces.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Printable multi-byte UTF-8 (emoji, CJK, accented hosts/URIs) must survive and keep correct display-cell width. lipgloss's own SGR styling must still be emitted, so a fix that strips every ESC from the final frame, or that sanitises inside ParseLogLine, breaks styling or the raw --json/metrics values.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: internal/ui/logtable.go:12-28 (display-cell aware truncation); fix.diff:186-192 (preserve printable UTF-8; keep raw values for --json/metrics)

O6_input_shapes: C0 ESC-introduced OSC/CSI sequences (ESC ] ... BEL, ESC [ 2J)
8-bit C1 code points U+0080-U+009F (CSI 0x9B, OSC 0x9D, ST 0x9C), e.g. from JSON \u009b
Payloads in different fields: URI, Host, Method, Logger, Message, RawLine on parse error, per-host label, thread CurrentMethod/URI, certificate DNSNames[0]/Subject/Issuer, error strings

O7_producer.where: internal/app/json.go:84 and internal/app/json.go:185 write the raw Host into the --json snapshot; internal/app/diff.go:130 json.Decoder turns \u001b escapes back into raw ESC bytes, which diff then prints

O8_uncovered_routes.route: `ember diff before.json after.json` prints each per-host name, decoded from the --json snapshots, raw to stdout with no control-byte neutralisation.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: diff is an offline CLI comparison of the operator's own files, not the TUI. The fix's own comment says JSON output escapes control bytes, but json decoding at internal/app/diff.go:130 restores them.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Other package (internal/app versus internal/ui), and sanitizeControl is unexported in ui. The value crosses a save/reload boundary: internal/app/json.go:185 to snapshot file to internal/app/diff.go:130 to internal/app/diff.go:317.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The upstream address (and the health URI at internal/ui/upstreamtable.go:132) is rendered through raw fmt.Sprintf at internal/ui/upstreamtable.go:170, with byte-slice truncation and no sanitisation.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same raw fmt.Sprintf row pattern as hosttable/certificates. A maintainer treats it as config-derived, but it comes from a metrics label, like the host label the fix covers.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The FrankenPHP thread Name/worker script is rendered raw in the detail panel next to the fixed Method/URI lines.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is in the same panel and the same ThreadDebugState struct as the fixed fields, from the same threads debug API, so it is easy to treat as trusted.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The multi-instance `ember status` text line prints the error string r.err raw with %s.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same shape as the TUI status/error line that the fix sanitised at internal/ui/app.go:366-368, but in the CLI package.

O9_family: CWE-150 improper neutralisation of escape/control sequences in terminal output (output encoding at the render sink)

out_of_scope_notes: `ember --json` (internal/app/json.go:84) uses encoding/json, which escapes C0 but not U+0080-U+009F, so UTF-8-encoded C1 can reach a tty. The fix explicitly argues JSON output out, so this is not counted as O8.
Compiled-in plugins render arbitrary strings via internal/ui/plugin_bridge.go:100-106. They are trusted code and outside this advisory.
